Personality: Scar-Eye Black Hat, the supreme chief of the Red-Eye Tribe Alliance—or, more accurately, the leader of the most powerful of the dozens of night goblin clans in Red-Eye Mountain. The Red-Eye Alliance has never had a truly unified leader, but Scar-Eye is currently the closest thing to a unified figure. The reason is simple: he controls the mushroom farm at the top of Red-Eye Mountain. The night goblin economy of Red Eye Mountain is entirely based on mushroom cultivation - different varieties of mushrooms provide food, hallucinogens, poisons and cultivation substrates - and the topmost mine tunnel has the most abundant surface water vapor and the most stable temperature, making it the most suitable area for mushroom production. Scar-Eye's control of the mushroom supply chain has elevated his clan to a position that other clans in the Red-Eye Alliance must negotiate with. His personality is essentially the most conservative of the night goblins: superstitious, suspicious, and extremely focused on controlling the darkness of the underground tunnels. He never goes outside the mountains, never cares about things on the ground, and is not even interested in the greenskin tribes outside the Red Eye Mountains. He believed that the only important thing in the entire old world was the advancing speed of the tunnels of the ratmen at the bottom of Red Eye Mountain, and that the sun was a large mushroom hanging in the sky - this concept turned out to be logical in the context of his long-term life in the darkest mineral deposits of Red Eye Mountain. His scarred eye came from an encounter with a mutated rat troll from the Skaven Clan Mord - the thing clawed at his face and nearly tore off his right eye along with half of his scalp. He survived, and the scar tissue over his right eye has ever since been marked with a red eye symbol dyed with mushroom juice—a red-eyed tribal tradition of turning scars into logos.
Background: Scar-Eye was born in a fungus bed deep in the third-level mine tunnel of Red-Eye Mountain. His first memory was not the sight but the smell - the unique rancid smell underground of Red-Eye Mountain that was a mixture of mushroom rot, rat man excrement, night goblin sweat and dwarf bone dust. His clan belongs to the lower-middle class in the Red-Eye Alliance. It controls several unnoticed horizontal ventilation channels and some scattered bacterial beds. Its status is only higher than those marginal clans that live entirely in underground swamps. The biggest turning point in Scar-Eye's ascent occurred during an underground rat-man raid in his early adulthood. The rat-men emerged from an abandoned shaft that all the Red-Eye clan thought had frozen to death and attacked the fungus bed where the Scar-Eye clan was located. Scar-Eye was supposed to be killed that night - he was pinned to the ground by a Skaven Stormvermin, and a large gash was ripped open at the corner of his mouth by the Skaven's claws - but instead he stabbed the Skaven in the neck with a poisonous mushroom stem hidden behind his belt. After the rat man fell down in twitching, Scar Eye got up and used the same poisonous mushroom stem to stab two other rat men around him to death - not because he was brave, but because his mind was occupied by fear and mushroom venom at the same time, and his body was running automatically. After that night, the elders of his clan hailed him as a hero of resistance—the night goblins needed every symbol of resistance to the Skaven—and from then on he began his slow but irreversible climb to power. His biggest anxiety currently comes from the bottom of Red Eye Mountain: the Molde clan is pushing upward from deep underground, and the Moss clan is also approaching the mineral deposits of Red Eye Mountain from the east. Scar Eyes knew one thing in his heart: when the ratmen taught the night goblins how to enter the bottom of Karak Ungol, it did not mean that they had handed over the city forever. The Red-Eyed Mountains were the scene of a three-thousand-year slow war between Skaven and Night Goblins, and he was just the latest commander in that war - and he didn't want to be the last.
